greet.text: Easy - you're no bandit. Brannoc, scout for the Riverwatch garrison. That circle behind me has been glowing since the new moon. The captain wants to know why. I want to know why it hums when I'm not looking at it.

choices.text: Maren says she told Riverwatch about the wolves.
I'll look into it.
What is this place?
Elves raised these stones, didn't they?
Riverwatch sends scouts out alone now?
(Keep your hood low.) Just passing through.
The stones are resonating. I've read about circles like this.
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Not my concern.

greet_again.text: Changed your mind about the stones?

choices.text: I'll look into it.
What is this place?
Can the garrison spare a healing potion? (30 gold)
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Any other work for the garrison?
Not yet.

lore.text: Older than Riverwatch, older than the road. The stories say the stones keep something asleep. The stories also say a lot of things after the third ale.

choices.text: I'll look into it.
Goodbye.

lore_elf.text: So your people's songs say. Then maybe you'll understand it better than a garrison scout. Will you take a look?

choices.text: I'll look into it.
Another time.

alone.text: Riverwatch sends scouts out alone when it doesn't have enough scouts. Which is always.

choices.text: I'll look into the stones for you.
Goodbye.

accept.text: Good. Touch the crystal if you dare - and look around the circle for anything that broke off it. Folk say shards of the old stones turn up after a storm.

choices.text: I'll be back.
I found three rune shards.
The crystal answered when I touched it. Fire ran up my arm.
Can the garrison spare a healing potion? (30 gold)
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Any other work for the garrison?
Still looking.

hint_shards.text: Fire. Of course it was fire. Then it's waking, whatever it is. Find what broke off it - three pieces, if the old tale is right.

choices.text: I'll find them.

decide.text: Three of them. Still warm. The scholars in Riverwatch would pay a fortune to study these... but I've heard the old tales too. Maybe they belong to the stones.

choices.text: Take them to Riverwatch.
They should go back to the stones.
I think I'll keep them. Someone will pay more than Riverwatch.
Let me think about it.

given.text: Sixty gold from the garrison purse, and the captain will hear your name. I hope we're not making a mistake. Before you go - look at the crystal again. It's been flickering since you took those.

choices.text: Farewell, Brannoc.

chose_stones.text: Then put them back yourself - I'm not touching that crystal. I'll tell the captain the circle is... being tended.

choices.text: I will.

waiting_on_stones.text: Still carrying those shards? The crystal's that way. I'll be here, at a respectful distance.

choices.text: The crystal showed me a thread of light, running north.
Can the garrison spare a healing potion? (30 gold)
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Any other work for the garrison?
Goodbye.

after_given.text: The scholars are beside themselves. Riverwatch owes you - I'll make sure the captain remembers it.

choices.text: The crystal showed me a thread of light, running north.
Can the garrison spare a healing potion? (30 gold)
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Any other work for the garrison?
Goodbye.

after_restored.text: The circle's light is steadier now. Calmer. Whatever you did, the humming's stopped keeping me up at night.

choices.text: The crystal showed me a thread of light, running north.
Can the garrison spare a healing potion? (30 gold)
Anything else I should know about out here?
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
I need a crate of the garrison's supplies.
Any other work for the garrison?
Goodbye.

kept.text: ...Keep them, then. But don't expect the garrison to look kindly on someone who pockets what belongs to the stones - or to Riverwatch. And look at the crystal. It's been flickering since you took them.

choices.text: Goodbye.

after_kept.text: You. I've nothing to say to you, and nothing to sell. The garrison remembers.

choices.text: The crystal showed me a thread of light, running north.
The bandit camp south-west of here is cleared.
Goodbye.

buy_potion.text: For a friend of Riverwatch? Thirty, and don't tell the quartermaster.

choices.text: Another, please. (30 gold)
That's all.

gift.text: The captain sent word: anyone who's done this much for Riverwatch gets the garrison's thanks in something more useful than words. Take these - and you'll always find a friend at the river gate.

choices.text: Thank you, Brannoc.

heard_of_you.text: The wolf-killer from the waystation! Word travels fast when it's good news for once. Then I know who to ask about the stones.

choices.text: Ask me what?

greet_stones.text: That circle behind me has been glowing since the new moon. The captain wants to know why. Will you take a look?

choices.text: I'll look into it.
Not now.

outlaw_line.text: Hm. You've a face I've seen on a notice board in Riverwatch. Or one like it. I can't be sure, and I've bigger problems than a poster. Help me with these stones and I'll stop trying to remember where I saw you.

choices.text: I'll look into it.
Not my concern.

scholar_line.text: Read about them? Then you already know more than me, the captain and the last three they sent. Look at the circle for me. Whatever you find, I want it in plain words.

choices.text: I'll look into it.
Another time.

bandits_info.text: Bandits. They've a camp south-west of the stones, three of them at least. The one in charge swings a mace and knows how to keep his guard up. The garrison pays a bounty if someone clears them out.

choices.text: I'll deal with them.
Any advice?
Not my fight.

bandit_advice.text: They're not wolves. They'll put a blade up when you swing, so lean on them: a heavy blow or a shield to the face breaks a guard. And watch for the glint before they swing.

choices.text: I'll remember that.

bandit_bounty.text: All three? Then the south road can breathe again. Here - the garrison's bounty, and I'll see your name goes in the captain's book.

choices.text: Glad to help.

mark.text: Brannoc turns the scrap over twice. "No. And I don't like that I don't. Garrison marks, guild marks, bandit scratches - I know them all." He looks past you at the circle. "But see the tall stone, near the top? Three lines through a ring. Same as this. Whatever emptied your wolf, it's got something to do with these stones."

choices.text: (Scholar) It isn't a brand. Something was drawn out of that wolf through the mark.
(Hunter) Its tracks came out of the forest to the north, in straight lines.
Then I'll look at the stones.
I'm already looking into the stones.
Goodbye.

mark_scholar.text: Drawn out. Like drawing water. ...Then someone's doing the drawing, and I'd like to know who before the captain asks me. Whatever's wrong at the circle, start there.

choices.text: Then I'll look at the stones.
I'm already looking into the stones.
Goodbye.

mark_hunter.text: North. The Thornwood, then. The garrison doesn't go in there, and the outlaws who live there don't come out to talk. If this leads into those trees, we'll need a better reason than a scrap of hide. Start with the stones.

choices.text: Then I'll look at the stones.
I'm already looking into the stones.
Goodbye.

drain_line.text: North. Into the Thornwood. Something's drawing on that crystal like a straw in a cup, and whatever's drinking is out in those trees. The captain won't send anyone in after a light in the sky. The outlaws live in there; if anyone's seen who's doing this, it's them. And they'd sooner put an arrow in a garrison coat than talk to one.

choices.text: Then I'll talk to them. I'm not wearing a garrison coat.
(Hunter) Same way the hollow wolf's tracks came from.
Not today.

drain_hunter.text: Then whatever emptied your wolf and whatever's drinking from the stones live at the same end of the same forest. I'll put that in my report, and the captain will ignore it. You won't, I think.

choices.text: (Leave)

crate.text: For the outlaws? Don't answer that. ...There's a cache under the oilcloth by my bedroll. Take one crate. I never saw you, and when the quartermaster counts crates, he'll blame me, and I'll blame wolves.

choices.text: Thank you, Brannoc.

end_intro.text: You're alive. The light over the forest went out an hour ago, and I've been standing here wondering which of us that was bad news for.

choices.text: (Show him the letter and the map.)

end_letter.text: He reads it with his lips moving, the way he reads orders. "The Pale Gate. I've heard the name. Old stories, the kind the captain doesn't let us tell on watch." He looks at the map for a long time.

choices.text: You kept your distance from the crystal. Smart.
You still think I should have handed over the shards?
What happens now?

end_kept.text: I still think you're a thief. I also think you're the only one who went into that forest. The garrison can hold both thoughts. Barely.

choices.text: What happens now?

end_brannoc.text: Now I take this to the captain, and she asks Riverwatch for soldiers it doesn't have, and the town says no. Then she asks me who did this, and I tell her. Don't be surprised if someone comes looking for you with a better offer than mine.

choices.text: (Leave)

licence.text: There's a hedge-mage living in the Thornwood, west of the outlaws' fire. No licence, no Collegium seal, and the captain's had complaints: lights at night, goats going missing. Bring her in. Fifty gold, and I don't have to go into those trees.

choices.text: I'll find her.
What if she won't come?

licence_force.text: Then she won't, and you come back and tell me so. I'm not paying you to kill an old woman over goats.

choices.text: I'll find her.
She came quietly. She says the goats were never her.
She was gone when I got there.
I never found her.

zora_paid.text: Quietly. Good. Fifty, as promised, and I'll tell the captain about the goats. Wolves, probably. It's always wolves.

choices.text: (Leave)

zora_gone.text: Gone. Convenient. ...I'll write "gone" in the report, then. No fifty for "gone", mind.

choices.text: (Leave)

end_hollow.text: He takes a step back before he means to. "Your eyes. In this light they look like that crystal's." He reads the letter anyway, lips moving. "The Pale Gate." He folds it into his coat. "I'll take this to the captain. I won't tell her about you. Not yet. Don't make me."

choices.text: (Leave)
